s1.syndrome_frame: Acute scrotal pain and swelling in a pediatric patient
salient_findings: Enlarged testis, epididymis, and infected appendages
Purulent foci on the surface of the sperm vessels
key_facts: 13-year-old boy presented with a five-day history of left scrotal soreness and oedema
No lower urinary tract symptoms
No major relevant medical or surgical history
Occult penis diagnosed based on penile characteristics
Other congenital anomalies of the genitourinary tract excluded based on imaging findings
Mild leukocytosis (18.5 × 10^9/L) on blood workup
Urine analysis was negative
Pus culture isolated P. aeruginosa, susceptible to ceftazidime and ofloxacin
Doppler ultrasonography showed an enlarged left testis with heterogeneous echo pattern and enhanced vascularity
Follow-up sonography showed heterogeneous echotexture in the left testis and epididymis
MRI at 60 days showed no enhancement in T2, indicating disappearance of the left testis
Pathological examination showed hemorrhagic infarction of the left testicular appendage and fibrocystic-like tissue with inflammatory cell infiltration

shortlist.label: Epididymitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with scrotal soreness and oedema, and Doppler ultrasonography showed an enlarged left testis with heterogeneous echo pattern and enhanced vascularity

shortlist.label: Orchitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had an enlarged testis, epididymis, and infected appendages, with purulent foci visible on the surface of the vessels

shortlist.label: Appendicitis of the testis
shortlist.why_kept: Pathological examination showed hemorrhagic infarction of the left testicular appendage and fibrocystic-like tissue with inflammatory cell infiltration

shortlist.label: Scrotal cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with scrotal soreness and oedema, and follow-up sonography showed heterogeneous echotexture in the left testis and epididymis

shortlist.label: Tuberculous epididymitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a chronic infection with P. aeruginosa, and tuberculous epididymitis is a rare but possible cause of chronic epididymitis

raw.rationale: The patient presented with scrotal soreness and oedema, and imaging studies showed an enlarged left testis with heterogeneous echo pattern and enhanced vascularity, indicating inflammation of the testis. The presence of purulent foci and tough, inseparable texture of the sperm vessels also supports this diagnosis. The MRI at 60 days showed no enhancement in T2, indicating disappearance of the left testis, which is consistent with orchitis leading to testicular damage.

rejected.label: Epididymitis
rejected.why: While epididymitis is a possible diagnosis, the imaging studies and pathological examination suggest that the testis itself is involved, making orchitis a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Appendicitis of the testis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with orchitis than appendicitis of the testis, which typically presents with a distinct appendage that is inflamed.

rejected.label: Scrotal cellulitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more localized to the testis and epididymis, rather than a diffuse infection of the scrotum.

rejected.label: Tuberculous epididymitis
rejected.why: There is no indication of tuberculosis in the patient's history, laboratory results, or imaging studies, making this diagnosis less likely.
